newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive 3.24 pct after inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive 3.24 pct after inflation data.

text.p: Istanbul shares drifted sharply lower on Tuesday morning following the release of January inflation data which brokers said boosted selling after the market's week-long consolidation.
The IMKB National-100 stood at 1,524 at mid-session, down 51 points, or 3.24 percent from Monday.
"Inflation figures came out above expectations. The market was already in a down correction and so the inflation news produced further falls," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

Turkish wholesale prices rose 5.6 percent in January against 3.4 percent rise in December and consumer prices rose 5.9 percent in January, up from 3.9 percent a month ago, the State Institute of Statistics said.
Bankers and brokers were mostly predicting the inflation data at between four and 5.3 percent.
The market index had lost 7.35 percent in the past week since last Monday's all-time high close of 1,700, after surging 74.2 percent and breaking 17 record closes from end-1996.

Brokers said cash drain from the stock market was also expected in the first half of this week due to an approaching holiday. Turkish markets will be closed next Monday and Tuesday due to the Islamic Ramadan holiday.
But they expected buying in the last two days of the week when settlements of transactions will be delayed to after the holiday.
